record.title: The $\mathbb{P}_4$ characterization conjecture for matroid representability
record.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an indeterminate, and define the partial field

$$
\mathbb{P}_4:= \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{Q}(\alpha),\{\alpha,\alpha-1,\alpha+1,\alpha-2\}).
$$

**$\mathbb{P}_4$ characterization conjecture.** A matroid $M$ is representable over all finite fields with at least $4$ elements if and only if $M$ is representable over $\mathbb{P}_4$. The statement is offered as a candidate after the preceding finite-field list conjecture could not be proved even for $k=4$; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: R. A. Pendavingh and S. H. M. van Zwam, “Lifts of matroid representations over partial fields”, arXiv:0804.3263 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3263

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

record.title: The four- and three-nuclei classification conjecture
record.statement: An $n$-nucleus is a minimal graph whose $n$-braid group is not a right-angled Artin group, whereas the $n$-braid group of every graph contained in it is a right-angled Artin group. **Nuclei classification conjecture.** There are exactly four $4$-nuclei, as shown in Figure~, and exactly ten $3$-nuclei, as shown in Figure~. This is a proposed finite classification of the exceptional graphs for braid indices four and three; the source gives no resolution beyond presenting the conjecture and the indicated figures.
record.source_name: Jee Hyoun Kim, Ki Hyoung Ko and Hyo Won Park, “Graph braid groups and right-angled Artin groups”, arXiv:0805.0082 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0082

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2008).

record.title: The quantum and delta grading conjecture for the Khovanov–Heegaard Floer spectral sequence
record.statement: Let $L$ be a link, let $\Sigma(L)$ denote the double cover of $S^3$ branched along $L$, and let $\{E^k(L),D^k\}$ be the spectral sequence whose $E^2$ term is the reduced Khovanov homology $\widetilde{Kh}(L)$ and which converges to $\widehat{HF}(-\Sigma(L))$. For each $k\geq 2$, consider the page $E^k(L)$ and its differential $D^k$. **Quantum and delta grading conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$, there is a well-defined quantum grading, respectively $\delta$-grading, on each $E^k(L)$, and the differential $D^k$ increases these gradings by $2k-2$, respectively $-1$. Such gradings would refine the spectral sequence beyond its known $E^2$ and $E^\infty$ terms and clarify how the limiting grading compares with the Maslov grading on $\widehat{HF}(-\Sigma(L))$.
record.source_name: John A. Baldwin, “On the spectral sequence from Khovanov homology to Heegaard Floer homology”, arXiv:0809.3293 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.3293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2008).

record.title: The Sprouts winning-strategy congruence conjecture
record.statement: In the Sprouts game, a two-player game beginning with $p$ spots in which the player making the last move wins, a player has a winning strategy for exactly one of the two players. **Sprouts winning-strategy conjecture.** The first player has a winning strategy if and only if $p$ is congruent to $3$, $4$, or $5$ modulo $6$. This is the original pattern conjectured from computer analysis of the game; the paper studies its extension from the plane to compact surfaces, while the general status of the pattern is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Julien Lemoine and Simon Viennot, “Sprouts game on compact surfaces”, arXiv:0812.0081 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.0081

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

record.title: Bialostocki's zero-sum permutation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive even integer, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ be zero-sum sequences with terms in $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. Thus

$$
\sum_{k=1}^n a_k=\sum_{k=1}^n w_k=0.
$$

**Bialostocki's conjecture.** There exists a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ such that

$$
\sum_{k=1}^n w_k a_{\sigma(k)}=0,
$$

where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\\{1,\ldots,n\\}$. The conjecture concerns pairing two zero-sum sequences so that their weighted inner product vanishes modulo $n$; the paper confirms it when the weights form an arithmetic progression with even common difference.
record.source_name: Song Guo and Zhi-Wei Sun, “On Bialostocki's conjecture for zero-sum sequences”, arXiv:0812.1724 (2009).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2008). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0710.3718](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.3718).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.1724

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

record.title: Komlós–Sós conjecture on degree-sequence conditions for tree embeddings
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $k$ be a positive integer. A tree with $k$ edges has $k+1$ vertices. **Komlós–Sós conjecture.** If at least $n/2$ vertices of $G$ have degree at least $k$, then $G$ contains every tree with $k$ edges. This conjecture is presented as a generalization of a theorem of Zhao and is part of the effort to characterize degree conditions forcing tree embeddings; the source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Embedding large subgraphs into dense graphs”, arXiv:0901.3541 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3541

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2009).

record.title: Kalai's separator conjecture for simple polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a simple $d$-polytope with $m$ vertices, and let $G_P$ be its graph. **Kalai's separator conjecture.** There exists a subset $V'$ of vertices of $P$ such that

$$
|V'|=O\left(n^{1-\frac{1}{d-1}}\right)
$$

and removing $V'$ from $G_P$ separates $G_P$ into two parts, each with at least $n/3$ vertices. The source presents this as a version attributed to Kalai and as a conjecture about vertex expansion; the variables $m$ and $n$ are inconsistent in the source statement, and no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Sandeep Koranne and Anand Kulkarni, “Combinatorial Polytope Enumeration”, arXiv:0908.1619 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.1619

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2009).

record.title: Eulerian descent-set distribution conjecture for marked cycles
record.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let ${\mathcal T}^0_n$ be the class of objects defined in the paper, let $D(\sigma)\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-1\}$ denote the descent set of $\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n$, let ${\mathcal S}_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $A_n(x)$ be the $n$-th Eulerian polynomial.

**Eulerian descent-set distribution conjecture.** For any $n$ and any subset $D\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-1\}$,

$$
|\{\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n\,:\,D(\sigma)=D\}|=|\{\pi\in{\mathcal S}_n\,:\,D(\pi)=D\}|.
$$

In particular,

$$
\sum_{\sigma\in{\mathcal T}^0_n}x^{\operatorname{des}(\sigma)+1}=A_n(x).
$$

The conjecture arose from experimental evidence and was checked by computer for $n$ up to $9$; the asserted distribution beyond those computations remains open.
record.source_name: Sergi Elizalde, “The number of permutations realized by a shift”, arXiv:0909.2274 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2274

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2009).

record.title: Lemke–Kleitman conjecture on indices of sequences over cyclic groups
record.statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the cyclic group of $n$ elements, let $d$ and $n$ be positive integers with $d\mid n$, and let $S$ be a sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$. For a subsequence $T$ of $S$, write $\sigma(|mT|_n)$ for the sum of the least positive representatives of the terms of $mT$, where $m$ is coprime to $n$. **Lemke–Kleitman conjecture.** There should exist a nonempty subsequence $T$ of $S$ and an integer $m$ coprime to $n$ such that

$$
d\mid\sigma(|mT|_n)\mid n.
$$

The case $d=n$ asserts that every sequence of $n$ elements in $Z_n$ contains a subsequence of index $n$. The paper states that this conjecture is false in general, giving counterexamples for $n=4k+2\geq22$, although related assertions hold under repetition hypotheses and are believed in some prime-order cases.
record.source_name: Weidong Gao, Yuanlin Li, Jiangtao Peng, Chris Plyley and Guoqing Wang, “On the Index of Sequences over Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:0909.2461 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2461

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2009); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: General bias-forcing conjecture for oriented even cycles
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph, let $n$ be its number of vertices, and let $e(D)$ be its number of arcs. For subsets $A,B\subseteq V(D)$, write $e(A,B)$ for the number of arcs from $A$ to $B$, and define

$$
bias(D):=\max\left\{e(A,B): A,B\subseteq V(D),\ e(B,A)\leq \frac{e(A,B)}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Even-cycle bias conjecture.** For each integer $k\geq 2$, there exists a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every oriented graph $D$ satisfying

$$
bias(D)<\varepsilon\frac{e(D)^{k/(k-1)}}{n^{2/(k-1)}}
$$

contains an oriented cycle of length $2k$.

This generalizes the paper’s proposed six-cycle bound and connects small orientation bias with the forced presence of longer even directed cycles. The source gives no indication that the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Omid Amini, Simon Griffiths and Florian Huc, “Subgraphs of weakly quasi-random oriented graphs”, arXiv:0911.3969 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.3969

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2009).

record.title: Freeness conjecture for the sharp transform of the planar binary tree algebra
record.statement:
Let ${\bf PBT}$ be the Loday–Ronco algebra of planar binary trees, and let ${\bf PBT}^\sharp$ denote its $\sharp$-transform. For each tree $T$ with at least two nodes and empty right subtree at the root, let ${\bf P}_T^\sharp$ be the corresponding sharp-transformed element.

**Freeness conjecture.** The algebra ${\bf PBT}^\sharp$ is free over the set ${\bf P}_T^\sharp$, where $T$ runs over trees with at least two nodes and such that the right subtree of the root is empty.

The claim describes a proposed free generating set for the sharp-transformed planar binary tree algebra. The supplied text gives no evidence that this assertion has been resolved.
record.source_name: F. Hivert, J. -G. Luque, J. -C. Novelli and J. -Y. Thibon, “The (1-E)-transform in combinatorial Hopf algebras”, arXiv:0912.0184 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.0184

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2009).

record.title: Linear-degree conjecture for Tverberg graphs
record.statement: Let $q\geq 2$ be a prime power, $d\geq 1$, and let $G$ be a graph on $(d+1)(q-1)+1$ vertices. A graph is a **$(d,q)$--Tverberg graph** if it has the corresponding Tverberg property for parameters $d$ and $q$. **Linear-degree conjecture.** There is a constant $k$ such that, whenever the maximal degree of $G$ is less than $kq$, $G$ is a $(d,q)$--Tverberg graph. The conjecture proposes a substantial improvement over the sufficient bound $D(D+1)<q$; its status is unclear from the supplied text.
record.source_name: Alexander Engstrom, “A local criterion for Tverberg graphs”, arXiv:1002.3447 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.3447

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2010). “Some skeleton of chessboard complexes, and in particular the chessboard complexes which are homotopy wedges of spheres, are shellable as proved by Ziegler .”

record.title: Cameron–Praeger conjecture on block-transitive 6-designs
record.statement:
Let a **block-transitive $6$-design** be a $6$-design whose automorphism group contains a subgroup acting transitively on its blocks; call the design **non-trivial** when it is not one of the standard trivial designs.

**Cameron–Praeger conjecture.** There are no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-designs.

This conjecture addresses the existence of highly symmetric Steiner designs. Cameron and Praeger had already proved non-existence of block-transitive designs for $t>7$; the paper establishes the stronger result that no non-trivial block-transitive Steiner $t$-designs exist for $t=7$ or larger, while the $t=6$ assertion is the remaining conjectural case in the supplied passage.
record.source_name: Michael Huber, “On the existence of block-transitive combinatorial designs”, arXiv:1003.1879 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.1879

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2010).

record.title: Sun's base- expansion conjectures
record.statement:
Let $n,m,k$ be positive integers with $m\geq 2$. For a positive integer, its base-$m$ expansion is the representation using digits from $0$ through $m-1$; a **non-zero digit** is a digit in this expansion that is not $0$.

**Sun's conjecture.** (I) There are at least $k$ non-zero digits in the base-$m$ expansion of

$$
\frac{m^k-1}{m-1}n.
$$

(II) The sum of all digits in the base-$m$ expansion of

$$
(m^k-1)n
$$
\nis at least $k(m-1)$.

These assertions generalize Sun's results for binary expansions and for prime bases, giving digit-expansion lower bounds for products involving geometric sums and $m^k-1$.
record.source_name: Hao Pan, “On a conjecture of Sun”, arXiv:1005.4368 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4368

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2010).

record.title: Depth-seven conjecture for edge rings of finite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph on the vertex set $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with $d\geq 7$, and let $K[G]$ be its edge ring. **Depth-seven conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{depth} K[G]\geq 7.
$$

The claim arises from computations showing that connected nonbipartite graphs with seven vertices have edge rings of depth at least seven. The preceding discussion presents it as a temptation rather than an established theorem; the supplied status gives no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Takayuki Hibi, Akihiro Higashitani, Kyouko Kimura and Augustine B. O'Keefe, “Depth of edge rings arising from finite graphs”, arXiv:1009.1472 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.1472

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2010).

record.title: Chartrand's existence conjecture for prescribed rainbow connection numbers
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $rc(G)$ and $src(G)$ denote its rainbow connection number and strong rainbow connection number, respectively. Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. **Chartrand's conjecture.** There exists a connected graph $G$ such that $rc(G)=a$ and $src(G)=b$ if and only if $a=b\in\{1,2\}$ or $3\leq a\leq b$. The conjecture asks whether the lower bound on $b$ in the preceding existence theorem can be removed; it was subsequently confirmed by Chen and Li, who constructed graphs with the prescribed parameters.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Yuefang Sun, “Rainbow connections of graphs – A survey”, arXiv:1101.5747 (2011).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1012.2693](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2693).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5747

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2011); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture
record.statement:
Let $0 \le k < d$ be integers, and let $r_0, \dots, r_k$ be positive integers. Suppose that $P_0, \dots, P_k$ are sets of points in $\mathds{R}^d$ satisfying

$$
|P_i|=(r_i-1)(d-k+1)+1
$$

for each $i$. **Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture.** There exists a $k$-dimensional flat $V\subseteq\mathds{R}^d$ and, for each $i$, a partition of $P_i$ into $r_i$ parts such that the convex hull of every part of every partition intersects $V$. This conjecture generalizes the central transversal theorem in the same way that Tverberg's theorem generalizes Rado's centerpoint theorem. Its topological and colorful generalizations are known when all $r_i$ are powers of the same prime $p$ and $p(d-k)=p\cdot\operatorname{codim}_{\mathds{R}}V$ is even; it remains open otherwise.
record.source_name: Nikola Sadovek and Pablo Soberón, “Complex analogues of the Tverberg–Vrećica conjecture and central transversal theorems”, arXiv:2408.14337 (2025).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1706.05975](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05975), [arXiv:0911.2692](https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.2692).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14337

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2024). “The topological generalization of the conjecture, along with a colorful version, has been confirmed by Karasev when all $r_i$ are powers of the same prime $p$ and $p(d-k)=p\cdot\codim_\R V$ is even; the conjecture remains open otherwise.”

record.title: Positive-coefficient conjecture for adjacent edges in independence polynomials
record.statement: Let $\mathsf K_n$ be the complete graph and let $Z(\mathbf I\mathsf K_n;\mathbf y)$ be the partition function of its independent-set system. For edges $e,f$, let $\Delta Z\{e,f\}$ denote the Rayleigh difference. **Adjacent-edge coefficient conjecture.** If $e$ and $f$ are adjacent edges in $\mathsf K_n$, then $\Delta Z(\mathbf I\mathsf K_n)\{e,f\}$ has nonnegative coefficients. The claim has been checked for $n\leq6$ and is open in general.
record.source_name: David G. Wagner, “Negatively correlated random variables and Mason's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0602648 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602648

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “A positive solution to the Big Conjecture would be a very good thing.”

record.title: The invertibility conjecture for self-complementary symmetric graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a self-complementary symmetric graph of order $n$, let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement, and let $G^{-1}$ denote its inverse under the graph operation used in the paper. **Invertibility conjecture.** The graph $G$ is invertible if and only if $n=1$ or $n\equiv5\pmod 8$; in that case, $G^{-1}=\overline{G}$. The statement is explicitly suggested by computer testing, while the supplied text gives no proof or disproof.
record.source_name: François Genest, “Eulerian graphs and local complementation”, arXiv:math/0701421 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701421

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

record.title: The Hom-complex realization conjecture for diameter-one graphs
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite simplicial complex, let $T$ be a finite connected graph, let $K_2$ be the complete graph on two vertices, and let $G_{1,X}$ be the graph obtained from $X$ by the construction in the paper with $k=1$. For a graph $H$, write $\operatorname{Hom}(K_2,H)$ for its Hom complex.

**Hom-complex realization conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{diam}(T)=1,
$$

then there is a homotopy equivalence

$$
\operatorname{Hom}(K_2,G_{1,X})\simeq X.
$$

This is the precise formulation of the proposed improvement from the general construction to the case of a complete graph with possibly some loops. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Anton Dochtermann, “The universality of Hom complexes”, arXiv:math/0702471 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702471

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2007).
